BiblicalUsage: The word means to long for, to pant after, and the psalm gives it its famous shape: as the hart pants after the water brooks, so pants my soul after God. Joel says the beasts of the field cry out to God in the drought, longing the same way.
TheologicalSignificance: Longing for God is as natural as thirst, and the hart by the brook is the picture of a soul that knows what it needs.
